title: Canada is getting older
hook: In 2016, Canadians aged 65+ outnumbered children under 15.
hookNote: July 1 estimates, 1971 to 2026; 2026 is preliminary. First year of the crossover in this series, which starts in 1971.

beats.text: Nova Scotia and New Brunswick: the first provinces where people 65+ outnumbered children under 15.
Canada: 5,919,685 people aged 65+, 5,868,008 under 15. The first year with more seniors.
Newfoundland and Labrador: median age 20.9 in 1971, the youngest province. 47.8 now, the oldest.

lines.text: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0005-01: population estimates on July 1, by age and gender. Statistics Canada Open Licence.

Columns show the share of each province aged 65+ (red) and under 15 (grey); province colour and the bars show median age. Every figure shown is a published value or a share of published counts; movement between years is animation. 2026 is preliminary.
This video shows how the age of the population changed, not why.

sourceLine: Source: Statistics Canada, Table 17-10-0005-01. Movement between years is animation.
method: Printed figures are published Statistics Canada July 1 estimates for the year on screen (median age; counts aged 65+ and under 15). Column heights are shares of published counts. Heights, province tints and bar lengths move linearly between consecutive years as animation only; in-between states are never printed. 2026 is preliminary.
